report:
**Conclusion:** Extensive scientific evidence shows that taking ibuprofen for COVID-19 does **not** worsen the infection or increase the risk of severe illness or death.

**Origin of the View:**
In March 2020, France's Health Minister publicly advised against using anti-inflammatory drugs like ibuprofen for COVID-19 (https://www.managedhealthcareexecutive.com/view/french-health-minister-stirs-questions-about-ibuprofen-covid-19). This recommendation stemmed from an early theoretical hypothesis that ibuprofen might upregulate ACE2—the receptor SARS-CoV-2 uses to enter cells—potentially facilitating viral entry or masking symptom severity (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7225250/).

**Scientific Evidence & Consensus:**
Subsequent real-world studies disproved this theoretical concern:

1. **Global Health Guidance:** Major public health agencies, including the World Health Organization (WHO), U.S. FDA, and European Medicines Agency, evaluated available data and confirmed there is no reason to avoid ibuprofen for COVID-19 symptoms (https://www.who.int/news-room/commentaries/detail/the-use-of-non-steroidal-anti-inflammatory-drugs-(nsaids)-in-patients-with-covid-19).
2. **Clinical Outcomes:** Comprehensive observational studies, systematic reviews, and meta-analyses examining thousands of patients found no association between ibuprofen use and higher mortality, intensive care admission, or worsened disease progression (https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s10787-023-01309-7).

**Summary:** 
The belief originated from an early, unproven theoretical hypothesis that was quickly refuted by clinical data. Healthcare organizations affirm that ibuprofen is safe to treat fever and pain associated with COVID-19 when taken as directed.
